newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain Treasury seen better off after bill auction.
newsitem.headline: Spain Treasury seen better off after bill auction.

text.p: Higher-than-expected demand for one-year and 18-month bills at a Spanish Treasury auction on Wednesday pushed yields to record lows, leaving the Treasury in good shape to face the heavy slate of debt maturing soon.
The Treasury alloted a total of 712 billion pesetas in one-year and 18-month bills, with a marginal yield of 4.975 percent for the former and 5.005 percent in the second maturity.
"The Treasury won on all sides. It reached the target to diversify issuance, making the average life of debt longer. It also reduced the one-year yield to a record low," a dealer said.
Dealers said they were suprised at total demand of more than 1.2 trillion pesetas in the two instruments, despite European market uncertainty ahead of the second round of the French election.
Analysts again applauded the Treasury's decision to issue 18-month bills, saying that investment trust demand was behind the aggressive appetite for these issues.

"The 18-month bills are ideal for FIAMM (investment trusts investing in assets no longer than 18 months)," a dealer said. "The fact that the Treasury issued more than 1.3 trillion pesetas of this maturity in only three auctions is not a problem. A good part of it will remain in funds' portfolios."
Other dealers added that uncertainty was prompting shifts in money in an already highly liquid market toward shorter bills, seen as a safe haven in comparison with the longer end.
But this trend met the Treasury's needs nicely.

"The Treasury is preparing this part of the curve which allows it to lengthen maturities to 1999 with issues in the second half of the year," said Alfredo Urrutia, economist at Societe Generale in Madrid.

In June and July alone, the Treasury is facing maturing bills and bonds for around five trillion pesetas, including around 760 billion pesetas in special debt, which was issued in 1991 in order to flush out undeclared black market earnings.
"The Treasury is preparing a cushion to face high (amounts of debt) maturing in June and July," said Alfredo Urrutia.
He added that from May to December public debt maturing stands at 12.3 trillion pesetas while Treasury financing needs amount at 2.13 trillion.
"The total to finance from May to December is 14.48 trillion pesetas, already covered for 2.3 trillion with May issuances (today's bills included)," said Urrutia.
At the end of April, the Spanish Treasury had also 2.92 trillion pesetas in its account with the Bank of Spain, of which it is likely to use some 1.5 trillion in coming months, analysts added.
